chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Hakeym and Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Masrouq, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked me about the people of Basra: 'What are they?' So I said, 'Murjiites, Qadiriyya, and Harouriyya'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah curse that nation of the disbelievers, the polytheists who do not worship Allah upon anything.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the people of Basra being Murjiites and Qadiriyya?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the dominant theological factions of Basra—specifically the Murjiites, Qadiriyya, and Harouriyya—by cursing them as a 'polytheistic' nation. This classification highlights the Shia scholarly view that deviations in core tenets like divine justice (*Adl*) and free will (*Ikhtiyar*) constitute a form of *Shirk* (polytheism) due to their failure to worship Allah according to the true understanding of His attributes. The Imam’s curse underscores the severity of these doctrinal errors in distinguishing the Ahl al-Bayt's theology from the broader Sunni theological schools of the era.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Hakeym and Hammad Bin usman, from Abu Masrouq who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws asked me about the people of Al-Basra: ‘What are they?’ So I said, ‘Murjiites, and Qadiriyya and Harouriyya’. So heasws said: ‘May Allahazwj Curse that nation of the Kafirs (unbelievers), the Mushriks (Polytheists) who are not worshipping Allahazwj upon anything’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn Hakim and Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from abu Masruq who has said the following: “

Once abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) asked me about the people of Basra in respect to who they are. I said, ‘They are Murji’a, Qadriah and Harawriah .’ The Imam said, ‘May Allah condemn such pagan nations who do not worship Allah on good grounds.’”
